body:
RossG12345 <rossg12345@aol.com> wrote:
:  You write, "The families are not important because they 
: were led by sick men who were trying to harm humanity with
:  their greedy and selfish "progress".

Scientists have no right to enslave mankind to their "progress".
Foresters have no right to rape mankind's forests for their own
profit.  Advertisers have no right to trick mankind with their
slickly produced lies.

It's of course unfortunate that innocent people might get harmed
for the work of deviant scientists and capitalists, but the
proximate cause is the deviant scientists and capitalists who
make their family open to this exposure through their immoral
behavior.

: ...Greedy and sick men who were trying to harm humanity 
: with their greedy and selfish "progress"?!   

: Your mistaken generalization concerning the victims is underlay
: by a more fundamental misapprehension -- that we would be
: better off as individuals if there were widespread famine and
: suffering.  Being opposed to advances in technology is one thing --
: urging the destruction of all modern organized society is quite 
: another.  And that is what Kaczynski does in his manifesto.

No one is advocating widespread famine and suffering.  There's no
reason to suggest that famine and suffering would result, except
to the extent that modern society is the sole source of junk food,
fast food, and soda, and therefore people are addicted to these
unhealthy and unnatural diet forms.

: Humanity begins with a single human.  If a person does not feel
: compassion toward the families of the people who were killed,
: then they should not be trusted to judge what is best
: for us as a society.

Someone who looks at the big picture sees more than what happens
on the news today.  Dr. Kaczynski is a student of history and was
trying to liberate humanity from a future of enslavement to
industrial-technological dependence.

That lunatic doctor promising to do cloning is judging what is best
for us as a society.  Do you trust him to let the cloning genie
out of the bottle?

124. The usual response to such concerns is to talk about "medical
     ethics." But a code of ethics would not serve to protect freedom
     in the face of medical progress; it would only make matters worse.
     A code of ethics applicable to genetic engineering would be in
     effect a means of regulating the genetic constitution of human
     beings. Somebody (probably the upper-middle class, mostly) would
     decide that such and such applications of genetic engineering were
     "ethical" and others were not, so that in effect they would be
     imposing their own values on the genetic constitution of the
     population at large. Even if a code of ethics were chosen on a
     completely democratic basis, the majority would be imposing their
     own values on any minorities who might have a different idea of
     what constituted an "ethical" use of genetic engineering. The only
     code of ethics that would truly protect freedom would be one that
     prohibited ANY genetic engineering of human beings, and you can
     be sure that no such code will ever be applied in a technological
     society. No code that reduced genetic engineering to a minor role
     could stand up for long, because the temptation presented by the
     immense power of biotechnology would be irresistible, especially
     since to the majority of people many of its applications will
     seem obviously and unequivocally good (eliminating physical and
     mental diseases, giving people the abilities they need to get
     along in today's world). Inevitably, genetic engineering will be
     used extensively, but only in ways consistent with the needs of
     the industrial-technological system.

: It might be found that they were just bitter at  being in a 
: backwater field ... being a lousy teacher ... facing the prospect
: of not making tenure as a result ... being emotionally out of 
: touch with people at the personal level ... and turning to vicious
: harmful pranks in order to get published after being unable to
: get his anti-tech views published otherwise.

You forgot to mention profound disgust at the meaninglessness of 
modern society, the complete powerlessness of anyone who isn't
wealthy, the domination of society by the elite for their own
purposes, and the lack of ambition that results in humanity
because they are beaten down by these forces.

Somehow you can't understand that Dr. Kaczynski tried to form a
revolutionary movement but no one had the ambition or vision to
participate.  Disgusted at the contributory negligence of his
colleagues to the aspect of the problems in the academic realm,
he thought it would be better to resign from his job and attempt
the necessary work by himself.  Not liking the degenerative weakness
in people is not being "emotionally out of touch", but rather it
shows good taste and a brave honesty.  None of them could ever
meet Dr. Kaczynski's high standards.  Look at his fierce
independence, strong will, and consistently good results in
everything he did in life.  His work from even his childhood years
bears these commendable attributes.

Your Judeo-Christian value judgments are without merit and furthermore
they reveal your biases and motivation.

H.W.
